messages.text:
"Build a 2D action platformer in the Metroidvania style (inspired by Dead Cells and Hollow Knight: Silksong) using pure HTML5 Canvas + JavaScript, in a single index.html file, ready to run with no installation.

CONCEPT
- One large, complex, interconnected world with NO \"level complete\" screen. Areas connect through doors, gates, and passages, and the player can freely backtrack.
- Multiple areas/biomes with different themes (e.g., forest, caves, underground city). Each area ends with a boss.
- Certain doors/gates are locked until the player defeats a boss or obtains an item/ability.
- Include a minimap and a world map that fills in as the player explores, plus checkpoints (benches/campfires) that save progress and restore HP.

CONTROLS (must be highly responsive, zero perceived input lag)
- Actions: move left/right, jump (hold for higher jump), attack, dash, wall jump, and drop through thin platforms.
- Mobile touch: virtual analog joystick on the left, action buttons on the right (Attack, Jump, Dash). Must support MULTI-TOUCH so the analog stick and buttons can be pressed at the same time.
- Also support gamepad (Gamepad API) and keyboard.
- Control feel: read input every frame, use a fixed-timestep 60 FPS game loop, coyote time, jump buffering, input buffering for attack/dash, and a dash with cooldown and brief invincibility frames.

COMBAT
- Melee attacks with clear hitboxes, short hit-stop, knockback, and screen shake.
- Player HP and invincibility frames after taking damage.
- At least 4 regular enemy types with distinct behaviors (patrolling, chasing, flying, ranged).
- At least 3 bosses with 2-3 attack phases, a health bar, and an arena that locks during the fight.
- Currency/item drops from enemies.

WORLD
- Tilemap-based maps built from data (arrays/JSON) so they are easy to expand.
- Smooth camera that follows the player and is clamped to area bounds.
- Area transitions through doors with a short fade.

VISUALS @COMMENT_BODY@ AUDIO
- Simple pixel-art style; if no assets are available, use placeholder shapes/colors and a parallax background.
- Simple sound effects (WebAudio) for attack, jump, dash, and taking damage.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
- Clean, modular code (Player, Enemy, Boss, Map, Input, Camera) with clear comments.
- Optimize for mobile performance (render only visible tiles).
- Main menu, pause screen, and Game Over screen with respawn at the last checkpoint.
- Save progress using localStorage.

WORKFLOW
Work in stages. Stage 1: the control system + player + one small playable area. After that, propose the next stages (enemies, first boss, doors between areas, map, new areas). Do NOT move on to the next stage until I say OK.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs

content.text:
Implemented **Stage 1** in `index.html` as a standalone, no-install Canvas game. It includes a small pixel-art clearing, responsive player movement, buffered jump/attack/dash, coyote time, wall jumps, drop-through platforms, keyboard/gamepad/touch controls with multitouch, sound effects, a pause screen, and a waystone checkpoint saved to `localStorage`.

I stopped at the requested Stage 1 boundary: **there are no enemies, bosses, connected biomes, or world map yet.** The JavaScript syntax check passed. I couldn’t capture a browser screenshot because Chromium isn’t installed in this environment.

Suggested next stages:
1. Add regular enemy types and combat drops.
2. Add the first boss and arena lock.
3. Connect areas with doors and gates.
4. Add the minimap and world map.
5. Expand into additional biomes and bosses.
